newsitem.title: USA: Peco could buy Maine Yankee on 'favorable' terms.
newsitem.headline: Peco could buy Maine Yankee on 'favorable' terms.

text.p: Peco Energy Co or another buyer for the Maine Yankee nuclear plant will probably buy the 910-megawatt facility on "favorable" terms, Central Maine Power Co's president said Thursday.
Maine Yankee's utility owners are have opened sale discussion with Peco Energy, and a Peco official told a Portland newspaper it expects any purchase would be made at a "low price."

"The observation that the terms will probably be relatively favorable to Peco, or some other buyer should one emerge, is substantial. We have to be realistic about this," CMP President David Flanagan told reporters after the company's annual meeting.

Flanagan said Maine Yankee's owners are still working on an economic analysis of the plant that will help determine a price for the facility and whether the plant should be reopened if a sales agreement is not reached.
Flanagan told shareholders that Maine Yankee's management is making progress in addressing safety concerns that kept the 910-megawatt facility in Wiscasset off-line since Dec 6.

"We still cannot say, however, whether Maine Yankee's costs, condition, and competitive outlook will permit resumption of its role as a major energy provider to the people of Maine and the rest of New England," Flanagan told the annual meeting.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by CMP, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro, five percent by Maine Public Service Co. and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
The owners have $150 million in outstanding debt, according to spokeswoman Maureen Brown.

Flanagan said CMP would like any sale agreement to have provisions allowing it to use Maine Yankee power as long as it remains a regulated utility. Maine lawmakers are considering a bill to deregulate the state's market by March 1, 2000.
Any sale would have to be approved by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. If approved, it would be the first sale of nuclear plant in the United States, according to NRC officials.

Maine Yankee is on the NRC's Watch List for troubled nuclear plants, after having had two years of expensive safety related problems. The owner's last year authorized $38 million in spending in 1997 to address safety problems identified by a special NRC inspection.
